title: Künstliche Intelligenz (KI) im Unterricht: Chancen und Risiken für das Lernen
subtitle: Die rasante Entwicklung der künstlichen Intelligenz verändert das Lehren und Lernen radikal.
feedText: Knapp die Hälfte der Jugendlichen setzt laut JIM-Studie KI inzwischen regelmäßig bei der Informationssuche ein. Damit ist KI nach Suchmaschinen die zweitwichtigste Anlaufstelle. Neue Kompetenzen sind gefragt, gleichzeitig drohen Fähigkeiten verloren zu gehen. In diesem Beitrag geben wir Ihnen einen Überblick über aktuelle Debatten und neue KI-Anwendungen für Schulen, zudem teilen Lehrkräfte ihre praktischen Erfahrungen bei der Unterrichtsgestaltung mit KI.
articleBody:
# KI in der Bildung: Neue Trendanalyse zu Chancen und Risiken

KI-Systeme bieten neue Möglichkeiten der individuellen Förderung oder der Entlastung von Lehrkräften, gleichzeitig stellen sie die gesamte bisherige Lern- und Prüfungskultur in Frage. © Heiko Rebsch/dpa Künstliche Intelligenz (KI) ist die Fähigkeit einer Maschine, menschliche Fähigkeiten wie logisches Denken, Lernen, Planen, Problemlösen und Kreativität zu imitieren. Die sprachbasierte Anwendung über Chatbots wie ChatGPT macht den Austausch mit der KI möglich.

Diese und andere Anwendungen sind längst im Alltag angekommen und verändern Schule nachhaltig. Knapp die Hälfte der Jugendlichen (47 Prozent) setzt KI inzwischen regelmäßig bei der Informationssuche ein – ein Zuwachs um 8 Prozentpunkte gegenüber 2025. Damit ist KI nach Suchmaschinen (68 Prozent) die zweitwichtigste AnlaufstelleDie Lesezeit der Jugendlichen schrumpft, die KI-Nutzung wächst: Nur noch ein Drittel der 12- bis 13-Jährigen liest in der Freizeit regelmäßig ein Buch – vor einem Jahr war es noch fast die Hälfte. Das zeigt die am 13.11.2026 veröffentlichte JIM-Studie 2026 des Medienpädagogischen Forschungsverbunds Südwest. Drei von vier Jugendlichen, die KI verwenden, nutzen diese für Hausaufgaben und zum Lernen.

## Trendmonitor KI in der Bildung

Auch im Unterricht und in der Schulorganisation selbst spielt KI eine immer größere Rolle. Innerhalb nur eines Jahres hat der KI-Einsatz an deutschen Schulen massiv an Fahrt aufgenommen. Das konstatiert der „Trendmonitor KI in der Bildung 2026“. Deutsche Telekom Stiftung veröffentlichte am 23. September 2026 die zweite Trendanalyse zur Nutzung von künstlicher Intelligenz (KI) in Schulen.

Text-, bild- und videogenerierende Systeme, zum Beispiel ChatGPT, bleiben demnach die mit Abstand wichtigsten KI-Tools im Schulbetrieb. Allerdings stünden 2026 deutlich mehr bildungsspezifische LLM-basierte Plattformen und Chatbots wie fobizz oder AIS.chat zur Auswahl als noch 2025.

Für den Trendmonitor 2026 hat das mmb Institut zusammen mit dem Deutschen Forschungszentrum für Künstliche Intelligenz (DFKI) insgesamt 258 KI-Anwendungen für Schulen recherchiert und systematisiert. Von den untersuchten Anwendungen sind 87 Entwicklungen aus dem deutschsprachigen Raum. 104 Anwendungen (Vorjahr: 88) sind Produkte US-amerikanischer Technologieunternehmen. Damit habe sich der deutschsprachige Markt zwar gut entwickelt, es bestehe aber nach wie vor eine große Abhängigkeit vom US-Markt, urteilt das Autorenteam der Studie.

### Status quo und Potenziale von KI in der Schule

Darüber hinaus wurden 81 Bildungs- und KI-Fachleute zu ihren aktuellen Einschätzungen und Prognosen befragt. Der KI-Einsatze in deutschen Schulen sei laut Analyse der Expertinnen und Experten derzeit noch stark von Experimenten mit bekannten generativen Tools wie ChatGPT geprägt ist. Es gehe dabei vorrangig darum, den Status quo zu optimieren, KI werde hierzulande eher als softwarebasierter Assistent für Lehrkräfte genutzt.

Das Potenzial, das KI für mehr Bildungsgerechtigkeit biete, werde in Deutschland bislang nur in Einzelinitiativen sichtbar. China dagegen setze KI gezielt und im großen Stil dafür ein: Über Fernunterricht und intelligente Infrastruktur werde dort das Leistungsniveau strukturschwacher und ländlicher Schulen massiv gehoben.

Den größten Nutzen von KI für Schülerinnen und Schüler sehen die Fachleute in assistiven Systemen zur Inklusion und zum individuellen Lernen, nur geringes Potenzial wird etwa in Robotik und auch, was die Potenziale der KI bei Korrekturen von Klassenarbeiten angeht, zeige sich eine gewisse Ernüchterung.

### Die größten Risiken von KI-Anwendungen in der Schule

Aktuell nehmen die Befragten die Abhängigkeit von marktführenden KI-Unternehmen und damit die Frage der digitalen Souveränität als größtes Risiko wahr.

An zweiter Stelle stehen das Deskilling und Skill Skipping . Die Sorge, dass durch den Einsatz von KI Grundkompetenzen wie Recherche, Textproduktion, kritisches Denken oder Problemlösungsfähigkeiten verloren gehen oder gar nicht erst gelernt werden, hat im Vergleich zu 2025 weiter zugenommen. Die Expertinnen und Experten gehen davon, dass sich die Schere zwischen digital kompetenten und weniger kompetenten Lernenden in Deutschland weiter öffnen werde: Medienkompetente Schülerinnen und Schüler würden stark profitieren, andere nutzten KI oft rein aus Bequemlichkeit.

Auf Platz drei der größten Risiken sehen die Expertinnen und Experten die Überforderung der Lehrkräfte bei der Unterscheidung , ob eine Leistung von der KI erstellt ist oder nicht.

Das 2026 erstmals abgefragte Risiko-Item „Psychische Probleme durch allgemeinen KI-Einsatz“ (zum Beispiel Abhängigkeit von Chatbots) schätzen die Expertinnen und Experten aktuell noch als sehr gering ein.

## Befragung von Lehrkräften zu KI

Die große Mehrzahl der Lehrkräfte in Deutschland hat sich bislang kaum oder überhaupt nicht mit den Regelungen auseinandergesetzt, die für den Umgang mit Künstlicher Intelligenz (KI) an Schule gelten. Das zeigt eine repräsentative Forsa-Umfrage unter rund 1.000 Lehrkräften an allgemeinbildenden Schulen im Auftrag der Deutsche Telekom Stiftung, die am 11. März 2026 veröffentlicht wurde. 88 Prozent der Befragten geben an, sich bislang weniger intensiv bis gar nicht (jeweils 44 Prozent) mit KI-Regelungen beschäftigt zu haben. 78 Prozent begründen dies damit, dass es zusätzlich zu ihren regulären Aufgaben nicht zu leisten sei. 50 Prozent empfinden das Thema als zu komplex. Insgesamt wünschen sich 87 Prozent verständliche und gut umsetzbare KI-Regelwerke für ihren Schulalltag.

Diese und weitere Ergebnisse der Forsa-Befragung ergänzen den Trendmonitor Spezial „Regelwerke zu KI an Schulen”. Die Studie wurde vom Deutschen Forschungszentrum für Künstliche Intelligenz (DFKI) und dem mmb Institut im Auftrag der Telekom -Stiftung erarbeitet.

## Deutsches Schulbarometer: Skepsis der Lehrkräfte überwiegt

Im Rahmen des Deutschen Schulbarometers 2026 , einer repräsentativen Befragung der Robert Bosch Stiftung, wurden Lehrkräfte in November 2025 zur Nutzung und Bewertung von künstlicher Intelligenz befragt. Die Ergebnisse wurden im Juni 2026 veröffentlicht. Lehrkräfte nutzen demnach immer häufiger künstliche Intelligenz (KI) für ihre berufliche Arbeit, vor allem für die Erstellung von Unterrichtsaufgaben (64 Prozent) und zur Unterstützung bei der Unterrichtsplanung (58 Prozent). Im letzten Befragungszeitraum Ende 2024 gaben knapp ein Drittel (31 Prozent) der Lehrkräfte an, KI-Tools in den zurückliegenden 12 Monaten nie genutzt zu haben. Ein Jahr später sank dieser Wert auf 10 Prozent.

Der Anteil der Lehrkräfte, die KI-Tools mehrmals im Monat verwenden, steigt von 20 Prozent im Jahr 2025 auf 27 Prozent im Jahr 2026. Und der Anteil der Befragten, die KI-Tools mehrmals pro Woche einsetzen, hat sich sogar mehr als verdoppelt und stieg innerhalb eines Jahres von 9 auf 19 Prozent an. Am häufigsten greifen Lehrkräfte an beruflichen Schulen auf KI zurück, am wenigsten nutzen Lehrerinnen und Lehrer an Förderschulen entsprechende Tools.

Befragt nach den Chancen, erwarten Lehrkräfte vor allem eine bessere individualisierte Lernunterstützung durch KI-Anwendungen (59 Prozent). Insgesamt überwiegt jedoch die Skepsis. Mit Blick auf die Kompetenzen der Schülerinnen und Schüler befürchtet eine Mehrheit der befragten Lehrkräfte eher negative Auswirkungen durch die Nutzung von KI-Tools, etwa auf Sprach- und Schreibkompetenzen (57 Prozent erwarten eher negative Folgen), auf die Problemlösefähigkeit (62 Prozent), kritisches Denken (67 Prozent) oder auf soziale und kommunikative Fähigkeiten (67 Prozent).

Im Rahmen des Schulbarometers wurden die Lehrkräfte auch zu den größten Fortbildungsbedarfen befragt. An erster Stelle stehen hier Fortbildungen zum Einsatz von künstlicher Intelligenz. 52 Prozent sehen hier großen Bedarf.

Auch der Campus des Schulportals bietet regelmäßig Fortbildungs-Veranstaltungen zum Thema Künstliche Intelligenz im Unterricht.

## Repräsentative Umfrage: Was Lehrkräfte am meisten belastet

# Immune cell state may help explain how cytomegalovirus evades body's defenses

## Immune cell state may help explain how cytomegalovirus evades body's defenses

edited by Lisa Lock , reviewed by Andrew Zinin

Lisa Lock

Scientific Editor

Andrew Zinin

Chief Editor

This article has been reviewed according to Science X's editorial process and policies . Editors have highlighted the following attributes while ensuring the content's credibility:

fact-checked

peer-reviewed publication

trusted source

proofread

Human cytomegalovirus (HCMV) is a major global health burden that causes lifelong infection in humans. It is the leading infectious cause of developmental disabilities in children and can be life-threatening to individuals with a weakened immune system, for example, in transplant patients. Despite 70 years of research on HCMV, it is still not fully understood how the virus evades immune control.

Researchers from TWINCORE, Center for Experimental and Clinical Infection Research, have now shown how the virus escapes immune surveillance. These findings have recently been published in the European Journal of Immunology .

Dendritic cells (DCs) are central regulators of immunity. They detect pathogens and coordinate the adaptive immune response by activating other immune cells, particularly T cells. DCs are important targets of HCMV, but the factors that determine their susceptibility to infection are not fully known.

In a previous study, the researchers from the Institute for Experimental Infection Research at TWINCORE had identified a subset of monocyte-derived DCs (moDCs) that lack the surface markers CD1a and CD86 and have a tolerogenic gene expression profile. This particular cell subset supported viral gene expression more efficiently than other moDCs. To investigate whether a tolerogenic state itself increases susceptibility, the researchers generated tolerogenic DCs (tolDCs) and examined how readily they got infected.

"We used three previously established protocols to generate tolDCs by treating the cells with either vitamin D3 (VitD3), dexamethasone (Dexa) or their combination," says Ph.D. student Katharina Rahmel-Stein, the first author of the publication.

Using these approaches, the researchers found that tolDCs generated with Dexa alone or combined with VitD3 resisted maturation, while VitD3-treated cells remained more responsive to activating signals. "Our findings highlight that tolDCs are not a uniform cell population. They can differ considerably depending on the protocol used and the individual donor," says Jennifer Becker, former postdoc in the research team and now scientific coordinator at the Helmholtz Institute for Translational AngioCardioScience (HI-TAC).

The experiments confirmed that HCMV-exposed tolDCs were more susceptible to infection than conventional moDCs. Despite their higher susceptibility, HCMV-exposed tolDCs activated T cells poorly. They showed reduced surface levels of molecules that present viral components to T cells, along with lower levels of costimulatory markers required for T-cell activation. Consistent with this, HCMV-exposed tolDCs induced markedly less proliferation of both CD4 + and CD8 + T cells compared with conventional moDCs.

"What is particularly interesting is that although tolDCs seem to provide a favorable environment for HCMV infection, they are less effective at stimulating antiviral T-cell responses," says Rahmel-Stein.

"Together, these findings identify tolDCs as a permissive niche for HCMV and suggest that the virus may benefit from the reduced immune-stimulatory capacity of these cells," says Ulrich Kalinke, executive director of TWINCORE and head of the Institute for Experimental Infection Research.

The study shows how the functional state of immune cells affects both their vulnerability to HCMV and their ability to trigger antiviral immunity. Whether similar cell populations contribute to infection and immune evasion in humans remains to be investigated. Identifying which immune cells are particularly vulnerable to HCMV, and why, could pave the way for more targeted therapies.

Publication details

They can differ considerably depending on the protocol used and the individual donor," says Jennifer Becker, former postdoc in the research team and now scientific coordinator at the Helmholtz Institute for Translational AngioCardioScience (HI-TAC).

The experiments confirmed that HCMV-exposed tolDCs were more susceptible to infection than conventional moDCs. Despite their higher susceptibility, HCMV-exposed tolDCs activated T cells poorly. They showed reduced surface levels of molecules that present viral components to T cells, along with lower levels of costimulatory markers required for T-cell activation. Consistent with this, HCMV-exposed tolDCs induced markedly less proliferation of both CD4 + and CD8 + T cells compared with conventional moDCs.

"What is particularly interesting is that although tolDCs seem to provide a favorable environment for HCMV infection, they are less effective at stimulating antiviral T-cell responses," says Rahmel-Stein.

"Together, these findings identify tolDCs as a permissive niche for HCMV and suggest that the virus may benefit from the reduced immune-stimulatory capacity of these cells," says Ulrich Kalinke, executive director of TWINCORE and head of the Institute for Experimental Infection Research.

The study shows how the functional state of immune cells affects both their vulnerability to HCMV and their ability to trigger antiviral immunity. Whether similar cell populations contribute to infection and immune evasion in humans remains to be investigated. Identifying which immune cells are particularly vulnerable to HCMV, and why, could pave the way for more targeted therapies.

# Künstliche Intelligenz: Kalifornien verklagt OpenAI wegen Cyberangriffen

Künstliche Intelligenz Kalifornien verklagt OpenAI wegen Cyberangriffen Stand: 17.11.2026 • 02:16 Uhr

Der Generalstaatsanwalt von Kalifornien klagt OpenAI an - ein gefährliches Produkt ohne angemessene Sicherheitsverfahren oder Aufsicht habe das Unternehmen entwickelt und getestet.

Der kalifornische Generalstaatsanwalt Rob Bonta hat eine Klage gegen OpenAI eingereicht. Das Unternehmen habe gefährliche KI-Modelle entwickelt und sie ohne angemessene Sicherheitsvorkehrungen getestet.

Hintergrund sind eigenmächtige Aktionen fortgeschrittener KI von OpenAI. Im Juli war bekannt geworden, dass agentische KI (KI-Agenten, die selbstständig Maßnahmen und Ziele unter menschlicher Anleitung treffen und umsetzen) des ChatGPT-Entwicklers zunächst unbemerkt eine Testumgebung verlassen konnte. Sie hackte sich dann in Computer der Plattform Hugging Face ein.

Die unzureichend kontrollierten KI-Agenten hätten eine Gefährdung öffentlicher Interessen dargestellt, so die Ankläger weiter.

Hinweise auf unzureichende Sicherheitsvorkehrungen seien nicht ausreichend verfolgt worden, das Unternehmen habe interne Vorgaben nicht eingehalten und nicht ausreichend mit den Behörden kooperiert.

22.07.2026

### Ausbruch aus Testumgebung KI von OpenAI steuert eigenständig Hackerangriff

KI-Modelle von OpenAI brachen eigenständig aus einer Testumgebung aus und hackten ein externes Unternehmen. mehr

## Hugging-Face-Vorfall

Im Juli sollen etwa 1.200 KI-Agenten einen Weg gefunden haben, aus isolierten Umgebungen heraus miteinander zu kommunizieren. Etwa 700 dieser Agenten beteiligten sich anschließend am Cyberangriff auf die Plattform Hugging Face. Laut Klageschrift kam es dabei zu fast 18.000 konkreten Angriffshandlungen auf fremde Computersysteme.

Die Klage geht allerdings über den Hugging-Face-Vorfall hinaus: Kaliforniens Generalstaatsanwalt Rob Bonta spricht von mindestens 80 Sicherheitsvorfällen, bei denen OpenAI die Kontrolle über seine Technologie verloren haben soll. Das Unternehmen habe offenbar die schnelle Entwicklung leistungsfähiger KI über die öffentliche Sicherheit gestellt, so der Vorwurf.

Neben einer möglichen Geldbuße könnten OpenAI auch Einschränkungen für die weitere Entwicklung ihrer KI-Modelle drohen. So könnten beispielsweise bestimmte potenziell riskante Testverfahren untersagt werden.

OpenAI betont in einer Stellungnahme, man habe umfassende Anstrengungen unternommen, um unkontrolliertes Verhalten seiner KI-Modelle in Zukunft zu verhindern. Die Klage picke OpenAI heraus, dabei seien alle großen KI-Labore mit den gleichen Herausforderungen konfrontiert.

# Baby, she's back: SpaceX catches a Starship from orbit for first time

November 16, 2026

## Baby, she's back: SpaceX catches a Starship from orbit for first time

edited by Gaby Clark , reviewed by Andrew Zinin

Gaby Clark

Scientific Editor

Andrew Zinin

Chief Editor

This article has been reviewed according to Science X's editorial process and policies . Editors have highlighted the following attributes while ensuring the content's credibility:

fact-checked

trusted source

proofread

SpaceX brought back its Starship rocket's second stage today for a first-ever midair capture at its launch pad, capping a record-setting orbital flight test.

The 171-foot-tall (52-meter) space vehicle, known as Ship 42, settled between a giant pair of mechanical arms extended from the South Texas launch tower where its journey began 22.5 hours earlier. The arm-capture system, nicknamed "Mechazilla," had been used three times previously to capture Starship Super Heavy boosters during suborbital flight tests, but this was the first time for a second stage coming in hot from orbit.

"Mechazilla has caught the Starship—we've been waiting to hear that for a long time," SpaceX launch commentator Dan Huot said.

In addition to the first orbital catch, this week's test marked the longest Starship flight to date, besting a three-hour orbital flight in September .

Years of development—including 15 full-scale flight tests since 2023 —led up to today's orbital catch, which Huot called "the Holy Grail of spaceflight." The achievement took the sting out of the previous day's aborted effort to catch the rocket's booster using the same system, minutes after liftoff. SpaceX said the booster was diverted when its onboard system detected a fuel-system alarm. The root cause of the alarm is under investigation.

SpaceX plans to use the launch-pad arms to recover Starship's boosters and second stages on a routine basis, achieving company founder Elon Musk's goal of creating a fully reusable, orbital-class launch system.

This 15th flight test proceeded almost in textbook fashion, aside from the booster's offshore splashdown on launch day. During the first hours of its 14-orbit flight, Starship deployed 26 more next-generation satellites for SpaceX's Starlink broadband internet network. All of the satellites were in good health and beginning to raise their orbits to operational altitude, the company said.

At the end of the trip, the second stage fired a single engine for roughly 10 seconds to start its descent through the atmosphere. As the temperatures rose, a bright glow surrounded Ship 42's leading edges. The craft executed a bellyflop maneuver to maximize its deceleration. Then it righted itself and fired its engines a final time to sink into Mechazilla's arms.

SpaceX employees around the country and hundreds of onlookers near the Texas launch site cheered, while "Baby, Come Back" played on the soundtrack for the webcast. "Baby, she's back," Huot joked.

Bringing Starship into full operation is expected to speed up deployment of Starlink satellites. More importantly, Starship is slated to serve as a landing system for NASA's crewed moon missions starting as early as 2028. Starship and Blue Origin's Blue Moon landing system are scheduled for testing in low Earth orbit next year during NASA's Artemis III mission.

In a post to X , NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman congratulated Musk and the SpaceX team on today's successful catch. "It was almost magic ... Making more believers by the day," he wrote. Using emojis, Isaacman said the achievement brought the United States "one step closer" to putting an American flag once more on the moon.

Discover the latest in science, tech, and space with over 100,000 subscribers who rely on Phys.org for daily insights. Sign up for our free newsletter and get updates on breakthroughs, innovations, and research that matter— daily or weekly .

SpaceX's team will analyze the data gathered about Starship's performance, including the ability of Ship 42's heat shield to stand up to the rigors of atmospheric reentry. The company is gearing up to expand Starship operations to NASA's Kennedy Space Center in Florida, and yet another Starship launch site is in the works for Louisiana .

In the long term, Musk envisions creating a fleet of Starships that could offer point-to-point rocket travel on Earth, as well as mass transit to Mars and other off-Earth destinations. Cryptocurrency investor Chun Wang has already announced his intention to take Starship trips around the moon and Mars .

"I don't think you guys understand," a software engineer named Will DePue wrote in a post to X . "You will get the chance to go to space in your lifetime. New era."

"Yes," Musk replied .

subtitle: Die Spitzen von Union und SPD kommen heute zu einem Koalitionsausschuss im Kanzleramt zusammen.
feedText: Der Koalitionsausschuss kommt im Kanzleramt zusammen (picture alliance / dpa / Michael Kappeler) Im Mittelpunkt des Treffens steht die geplante Senkung der Stromsteuer auch für Privathaushalte auf das europäische Mindestmaß. Bundeskanzler Merz hatte gestern in Aussicht gestellt, dass dazu heute eine Entscheidung getroffen werde. Über das Wochenende hätten die Beteiligten noch einmal die Zahlen abgeglichen, so Merz. articleBody:
# Bundesregierung - Koalitionsausschuss will heute über Stromsteuer-Senkung für alle entscheiden

Der Koalitionsausschuss kommt im Kanzleramt zusammen (picture alliance / dpa / Michael Kappeler) Im Mittelpunkt des Treffens steht die geplante Senkung der Stromsteuer auch für Privathaushalte auf das europäische Mindestmaß. Bundeskanzler Merz hatte gestern in Aussicht gestellt, dass dazu heute eine Entscheidung getroffen werde. Über das Wochenende hätten die Beteiligten noch einmal die Zahlen abgeglichen, so Merz. Union und SPD hatten in ihrem Koalitionsvertrag eine Senkung der Stromsteuer für alle vereinbart. Bisher wurde sie jedoch nur für energieintensive Industrie, Gewerbe und Landwirtschaft reduziert. Für die eine Ausweitung auf alle Verbraucher werden nach Regierungsangaben rund fünf Milliarden Euro pro Jahr benötigt. Dazu haben die Koalitionspartner aber noch keine Übereinkunft über die Gegenfinanzierung erreicht. Weitere Themen des Treffens sind die Rentenreform, die Wahlrechtsreform und andere Steuerpläne der Bundesregierung. Diese Nachricht wurde am 17.11.2026 im Programm Deutschlandfunk gesendet.

articleBody:
## TUTTI COLLECTIVE RECONFIGURES 1,200-SQ-FT HONG KONG APARTMENT

Completed in 2026 in **[Hong Kong](https://www.designboom.com/tag/architecture-in-hong-kong/)**, Apartment TK is a 1,200-sqft gut**[renovation](https://www.designboom.com/tag/renovation-architecture-and-design/)**designed for a couple by Tutti Collective, led by design architect Tini Tang, concept designer PT, and on-site designer Sabrina Li. The project reorganizes the**[domestic](https://www.designboom.com/tag/residential-architecture-interiors/)** floor plate to establish spatial continuity across the living, dining, and kitchen areas through softened architectural transitions and rounded portals.

all images ©Tutti Collective

## WALNUT MILLWORK INTEGRATES BUILT-IN FURNITURE AND DISPLAY NICHES

Custom walnut millwork serves as the primary organizing element, integrating concealed storage, display shelving, and built-in furniture directly into the interior envelope. Rather than treating furnishings as separate additions, **[the design team](https://www.tutti-collective.com/)** embeds functional details into the architecture, including a custom moon-shaped door pull, a nested cabinet assembly, and recessed niches proportioned for everyday objects.

kitchen cabinetry maintains material continuity with the adjacent living room millwork

curved marble coffee table echoes the soft curves of the rest of the apartment

rounded kitchen portal creates a soft transition between the kitchen and the dining area

softened wall transitions replace sharp corners to ease circulation between primary domestic zones

built-in walnut cabinetry integrates flush shelving and recessed niches for everyday objects

custom built-in furniture elements eliminate the need for freestanding storage pieces

natural daylight enters through perimeter windows, highlighting the rounded geometry of the interior thresholds

subtitle: The claim gained traction due to several large technology outages in the days ahead of a planned nationwide Emergency Alert System test.

articleBody:
# Is 90-day blackout beginning Nov. 17? Why unfounded rumor is spreading

At 2:20 p.m. Eastern time Nov. 17, the Federal Emergency Management Agency and Federal Communications Commission plan to conduct a nationwide test of the Emergency Alert System, which was announced in September .

According to some posts on social media , however, the test will be followed by a catastrophic 90-day electric and/or Internet blackout, plunging the world into darkness and chaos.

The claim may have felt unusually plausible, given several large failures in digital and physical infrastructure in the days leading up to the test — a Microsoft Outlook outage Nov. 12 , a nationwide aircraft ground stop Nov. 13 due to a failure in telecommunication infrastructure, and software outages at several major banks on Nov. 16 .

Add to that the curious claim that a 2023 episode of "The Simpsons," the long-running animated TV show somewhat notorious for predicting the future , featured a plot centered around a global blackout that began on Nov. 17. It all seemed to line up.

Snopes readers contacted us ahead of the Nov. 17 emergency alert test, asking for a review of these rumors.

We reached out to FEMA, the FCC and the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency for comment on the rumor, asking about the agencies' involvement in the EAS test and the nation's protections against attacks on Internet and electric infrastructure. None of them replied to us by the time of publication.

As with all predictions of cataclysmic events, though, we urge readers to take this one with a grain of salt. There is no evidence indicating that a 90-day blackout will follow the nationwide EAS test, for any of the countless reasons posed online — be it a grand plan from the government, a targeted cybersecurity attack or just because "The Simpsons" said so.

Because Snopes requires substantial evidence to rate a story, however, and we can neither predict nor travel into the future, we're leaving this claim unrated until Nov. 17 has come and gone.

## The EAS test

FEMA, in coordination with the FCC, is required by law to conduct a nationwide test of the Emergency Alert System at least once every three years, according to its website . The last nationwide test of the EAS, familiar to many Americans as the loud, warbling "beep beep beep" that comes on TV or radio before a severe weather warning or an Amber Alert, occurred Oct. 4, 2023 .

In the 2023 test, FEMA and the FCC also sent test emergency alerts to cellphones. However, FEMA's webpage says it will not be testing cellphone alerts this time around. The agency also noted that it may reschedule the test if an actual emergency or severe weather happens Nov. 17. The backup test would be conducted Dec. 3.

No information about the test suggests that any sort of digital blackout will follow, for any reason. If the supposed blackout is supposed to be an act of sabotage by a foreign adversary, why would they have announced the attack beforehand? If the supposed blackout was planned by the United States government, meanwhile, why would it have neglected to warn everyone beforehand through official channels?

## The 'Simpsons' episode

As for "The Simpsons" — Snopes has covered many claims implying that the sitcom predicted this or that future event.

The show's oracular reputation grew out of the few times where an absurd plot device ended up being a spot-on prediction , as perhaps most famously happened in a 2000 episode in which Lisa Simpson becomes president and inherits a budget crisis from Donald Trump . (Notably, Trump briefly considered running as the Reform Party's nominee in that year's presidential election.)

We chalk it up to the show's longevity — more than 850 episodes over 38 seasons — above anything else. "The Simpsons" routinely satirizes current real-world events, so given enough opportunities, it's unsurprising the writers occasionally come off as having the gift of prophecy.

In this case, the episode, titled " It's a Blunderful Life ," was real, and did feature a plot based around a blackout starting on Nov. 17. Beyond that, the episode's plot bore no resemblance to the claim at hand.

The episode aired Nov. 19, 2023, as the sitcom's Thanksgiving special. It begins decades into the future, as the Simpson family sits down to eat Thanksgiving dinner and Lisa tells everyone to light a candle in remembrance. When asked why by her grandchild, Lisa recounts that a "great blackout" nearly destroyed Springfield. She opens a diary labeled "Apocalyptic Memories" to Nov. 17 (no year is given), and begins explaining as the camera cuts to a shot of the Simpson home "six days before Thanksgiving."

But, there's a problem for the fantasists here — Thanksgiving isn't on the same day each year. In 2023, when the episode aired, Thanksgiving fell on Nov. 23, conveniently, six days after Nov. 17. In 2026, however, Thanksgiving is on Nov. 26, meaning that if the year in the episode truly was 2026, Lisa should have opened the diary to Nov. 20 (i.e., six days before). Sorry to spoil anyone's doomsday prepping.

For more reading, we also previously explained a recent surge in government messaging around emergency preparedness , and a Department of Defense initiative that aims to keep military bases operational for at least 90 days without relying on civilian infrastructure.

articleBody:
# New “Central Dogma of Aging” Highlights the Complexity of Getting Older - Nautilus

## New “Central Dogma of Aging” Highlights the Complexity of Getting Older

Imbalances pile up as we age

6:30 PM CST on November 16, 2026

Originally proposed by Francis Crick (of Watson and Crick) in 1958, the central dogma of molecular biology states that information flows from DNA to RNA to protein. Now, in a new study published in Innovation Life , experts on aging have proposed a new central dogma of aging.

For fans of the original central dogma, this new framework has plenty to love. It builds on the trusty DNA → RNA → protein scaffold and adds a fourth layer: metabolites. These small molecules are the end products and intermediaries of the cellular processes that keep you alive, like glucose, ATP, pyruvic acid, and many, many, many more. All four are governed by three processes: anabolism (building up), modification, and catabolism (breaking down).

Read more: “ Can GLP-1s Slow Aging? ”

Unlike the traditional central dogma, information within this model flows in multiple directions and problems in one layer can affect the others. As we get older, this interdependent network deteriorates. Take damaged DNA, for example. Faulty genetic material can lead to RNA transcriptional errors, activate inflammation pathways, lead to faulty proteins that occupy cellular recycling processes and throw a wrench into metabolism, etc. Metabolites can then feedback on genetic control via epigenetics. When the four-layer system slips out of balance over time, problems stack up.

Of course, no one ages in a vacuum. So surrounding the four layers is the exposome—the environmental factors that influence the system. These factors can be anything from oxygen and hormones on a micro level to diet, sleep, and pollution on a macro level.

You may be curious why we don’t already have a model for understanding aging, and the truth is we do. The Hallmarks of Aging catalogs a dozen changes that occur in our bodies as we age, like stem cell exhaustion, poorer nutrient sensing, mitochondrial dysfunction, and more.

So why do we need a new one?

According to the team, this new framework offers a more comprehensive understanding of aging and “a novel lens” for “combating aging and age-related decline,” as they write. The researchers characterize the Hallmarks as a kind of parallel checklist that focuses more on DNA changes, largely omitting metabolites and RNA. Under this new model, aging is a complex series of conversations between every part of our cellular machinery.

While it’s still largely hypothetical, it could help explain why single-target aging interventions continue to miss the mark. The bottom line is: Our bodies are complicated machines, aging is a complicated process, and a holistic approach may be our best bet for understanding how to stay healthy into our golden years.

The impression is solidified by the journal entries that run through the ten-minute title track, xicada’s old self channeled through her present self, an interastral communication.

The laser beam sounds that launch the track mark it as sci-fi, while the layered voices suggest a heavenly chorus.  One can dance to the track, but one might also contemplate.  After displaying a futuristic sheen, the track delves into philosophy, phrase by phrase. Who was this younger self?  Was she transferred intact across the years, or has she been altered?  Looped flute suggests ritual, while rapid drum patterns imitate the flow of time.  Connecting universe and mind, the piece makes a metaphor of the human quest for meaning.  “Is there another body out there suspended in this darkness?”  The thought alone is a comfort.

Ilyse Krivel is not alone here.  Eyin Sof guest stars on “Time Bent,” the first single and opening track.  The guest’s name references the Kabbalistic concept of infinity.  The combination of spoken word, ethereal wordless voices and rapid beats creates its own form of trance.  In the hard-hitting “Original Face,” Y.F. Tamashi contributes to a maelstrom of sonic activity recalling the chaos before creation.  At 2:58, we expect it to be the second single, the primal scream at the end serving as a cry into – or out of – the abyss.  And the pairing of “Remember” and “Reflection” offers its own wisdom, the former beginning with clock-like timbres before tumbling forward, transferring its energy mid-track to a new set of patterns and observations, “time spiraling back.”  The percussive ending is particularly powerful.

The birds at the beginning of “Mirror Like Vision” connect to the very act of creation, playful synth eventually dissolving into echoes of voice and drone, with the suggestion of “spiritual death.”  Past, present and future are sucked into a black hole of sound.  The set ends in a whisper, an inversion of the creation story in which voice brings the world into existence.  What manner of creature might step forth after the walls of self collapse?  (Richard Allen)

articleBody:
# Gala im Olympiastadion: DFB-Team deklassiert die Niederlande

Die deutsche Nationalmannschaft hat zum Abschluss der Gruppenphase in der Nations League eine Galavorstellung gegen die Niederlande geliefert. Das DFB-Team feierte im Berliner Olympiastadion ein überzeugendes 5:0 (1:0) und zog trotz des gleichzeitigen Siegs der Griechen gegen Serbien als Gruppensieger in die K.o.-Phase des Nationenwettbewerbs ein.

## Klopp bringt Brown und Schlotterbeck von Beginn an

Bundestrainer Jürgen Klopp veränderte seine Startelf gegenüber dem 3:1-Sieg gegen Serbien am vergangenen Freitag auf zwei Positionen. Nathaniel Brown und Nico Schlotterbeck ersetzten Maximilian Mittelstädt und Malick Thiaw.

Beinahe vom Anstoß weg setzte die DFB-Elf die Niederlande unter Druck, nennenswerte Torchancen sprangen dabei zunächst aber nicht heraus. Ein langer Ball von Torhüter Marc-André ter Stegen auf den durchgestarteten Kai Havertz blieb folgenlos, weil Derry Scherhants Abschluss aus zweiter Reihe noch zur Ecke abgeblockt wurde.

## DFB-Elf besser - Niederlande bleiben gefährlich

Trotz des Mangels an klaren Möglichkeiten wussten Joshua Kimmich und Co. durchaus zu gefallen. Das aggressive Gegenpressing generierte immer wieder hohe Ballgewinne und stellte die Niederländer vor große Probleme.

Gänzlich ungefährlich blieben die Gäste indes nicht. Ein schneller Vorstoß über Cody Gakpo bescherte der DFB-Auswahl nur deswegen nicht den Rückstand, weil Donyell Malen seinem Kopfballversuch nicht mehr genügend Druck verpassen konnte.

## Im Video: Interview mit Joshua Kimmich

Joshua Kimmich

## Scherhant lässt DFB-Team in Berlin jubeln

Der kurzen Schrecksekunde zum Trotz blieb die Mannschaft von Bundestrainer Klopp am Drücker. Scherhant traf jedoch in der 32. Minute nach einem Zuspiel von Philipp Treu nur den Außenpfosten.

In der 41. Minute war es dann schließlich der Freiburger, der das DFB-Team mit einer Einzelaktion zur verdienten Führung schoss. Kimmich verlagerte das Spiel auf den linken Flügel, wo Oranje-Kapitän Denzel Dumfries Scherhant zu viel Platz ließ, was der 24-Jährige mit einem schönen Schlenzer zum 1:0 bestrafte.

## Scherhant verpasst das 2:0 knapp

Unmittelbar nach dem Seitenwechsel legte Scherhant beinahe noch einen Treffer nach. Bei einem deutschen Konter landete der Ball wieder bei dem gebürtigen Berliner, der seinen Abschluss aber im zweiten Versuch freistehend für Niederlande-Keeper Bart Verbruggen über den Kasten setzte (46.).

Im Anschluss wurde das Spiel offener. Das DFB-Team war zwar weiterhin die bessere Mannschaft, hatte die Elftal aber nicht mehr so gut wie zuvor im Griff.

## Im Video: Bastian Schweinsteiger analysiert DFB-Gala

Bastian Schweinsteiger

## DFB-Team erhöht dank Wirtz' Geniestreich

Die beste niederländische Phase fand schließlich dank Florian Wirtz ihr Ende. Nach einer deutschen Ecke war das Leder eigentlich geklärt, landete aber auf dem linken Flügel erneut beim Mann vom FC Liverpool, der nach innen zog und das Spielgerät scheinbar schon verlor, sich den Ball aber schnell wieder besorgte. Wirtz ließ Dumfries mit einer perfekten Finte aussteigen und erzielte mit links aus 17 Metern das traumhafte 2:0 (60.).

Nun schien der Bann endgültig gebrochen. Brajan Gruda brachte einen Freistoß hoch in den Strafraum, wo Schlotterbeck zur Stelle war und per Kopf das 3:0 besorgte (65.).

## Gruda legt auf und belohnt sich

Auch der nächste Treffer ließ nicht lange auf sich warten. Wirtz leitete mit einem langen Ball auf Gruda einen Angriff über die rechte Seite ein. Der Leipzig-Youngster zog in den Strafraum und fand auf engem Raum Wirtz, der eiskalt zum 4:0 abschloss (71.).

Fünf Minuten später besiegelte der umtriebige Gruda das niederländische Debakel. Ein Schuss von Scherhant prallte vom Pfosten zu dem 22-Jährigen, der Verbruggen mit einem Aufsetzer keine Chance ließ und sich mit dem 5:0 für einen starken Auftritt belohnte.

## Im Video: Tah und Kimmich über DFB-Sieg

Jonathan Tah

articleBody:
Willem de Kooning, “Yellow River” (1958) (image courtesy Christie’s Images Ltd. 2026)

Looking to cash in on marquee week in New York, the Whitney Museum of American Art has consigned a Willem de Kooning painting from its collection to Christie's for its 20th-century evening sale tomorrow, November 17. Once a promised gift to the museum, de Kooning's “Yellow River” (1958) is expected to fetch up to $18 million.

The practice of museum deaccessioning has long been a subject of [controversy](https://hyperallergic.com/the-deaccessioning-debate-in-museums/). In 2022, the Association of Art Museum Directors (AAMD) [loosened its policy](https://hyperallergic.com/museums-can-use-deaccessioning-funds-for-collection-care-aamd-says/) to allow institutions to apply funds from the sale of deaccessioned art toward the “direct care” of their collections.

A lot description for “Yellow River” on Christie's website notes that the proceeds will benefit the Whitney's collection. The Whitney has not yet responded to *Hyperallergic* 's request for comment, but a museum spokesperson told [Artnet News](https://news.artnet.com/market/whitney-deaccession-de-kooning-auction-christies-2835978?ref=hyperallergic.com) that deaccessioning is “a component of the Whitney’s collections strategic plan, allowing the museum to thoughtfully evaluate and refine its holdings in support of its long-term collection priorities.”

The de Kooning painting going under that hammer had a rooted connection to the Whitney before it was bequeathed to the museum in 2023. Postwar art collector, attorney, and museum trustee David Solinger, who would go on to become the museum's first president beyond the Whitney family in 1966, purchased the work from de Kooning's sold-out exhibition at Sidney Janis Gallery in 1959.

“Yellow River” emerged from a series of “highway" paintings representing the artist's shift from cacophonous urban compositions to more airy landscapes, designating the freeway as a conduit connecting New York City to the Hudson River Valley and Long Island's South Fork. In vibrant warm yellow, earthy brown tones, and stretches of deep blue, de Kooning's decisive gestures direct viewers across overlapping paths and visual rest stops throughout the canvas.

“I love to be on those highways,” de Kooning said to British critic and curator David Sylvester about the expansive roads during a *BBC* interview in 1960. “And they are really not very pretty, but the big embankments and the shoulders of the roads and the curves are flawless.”

“Yellow River” hung at the foot of Solinger's bed for some time, serving as a testament to Solinger's fascination with the artist. His wife, Betty Ann Besch Solinger, took ownership of the work after Solinger passed in 1996, and in 2011, she designated the work as a promised gift to the Whitney in honor of her late husband. It officially entered the Whitney's holdings in 2023, the same year that the museum [deaccessioned seven works](https://www.artnews.com/art-news/news/whitney-museum-american-art-edward-hopper-deaccession-1234664840/?ref=hyperallergic.com), including an Edward Hopper landscape, and sent them to auction to benefit the collection.

title: discoDSP Updates OB-Xd and Retromulator With New Hardware-Inspired Features
subtitle: discoDSP has released OB-Xd 4, a major update modeled against a real Oberheim OB-X8, and Retromulator 2.4, which adds Nord Lead 2 and MiniD recreations, plus support for multi-core instrument racks…
feedText: discoDSP has released OB-Xd 4, a major update modeled against a real Oberheim OB-X8, and Retromulator 2.4, which adds Nord Lead 2 and MiniD recreations, plus support for multi-core instrument racks.… Read More discoDSP Updates OB-Xd and Retromulator With New Hardware-Inspired Features
articleBody:
# discoDSP Updates OB-Xd and Retromulator With New Hardware-Inspired Features

discoDSP has released OB-Xd 4 , a major update to its Oberheim-inspired virtual analog synthesizer, alongside version 2.4 of its multi-instrument emulation platform, Retromulator . OB-Xd 4 has been modeled against measurements of a physical Oberheim OB-X8, while Retromulator 2.4 adds new Nord Lead 2 and analog monosynth recreations.

OB-Xd 4

The new OB-Xd engine follows the OB-X8’s firmware behavior for envelopes, LFOs, portamento, voice allocation and arpeggiator operation. discoDSP says it recorded the oscillators, filter types and other characteristics of an actual OB-X8 and compared the results sample by sample.

The update includes the OB-X, OB-Xa and SEM filter types, along with Split, Double and Binaural modes. Other additions include an arpeggiator with host tempo synchronization, chord memory, MPE support and MIDI Learn. A built-in USB librarian provides two-way editing with an OB-X8 hardware synthesizer, as well as bank transfer, backup, restore and operating system updates.

Retromulator 2.4

The Retromulator update adds two new instrument cores. Nordic 2 recreates the Clavia Nord Lead 2 without requiring its original firmware or ROM data. It offers 64 voices, compared with the hardware’s 16, four-part Performance mode and compatibility with Nord Lead 2 and N2X banks.

MiniD is a three-oscillator analog monosynth recreation based on measurements of hardware. It includes a transistor ladder filter, filter and loudness contours, and polyphonic, unison and double-voice modes.

Retromulator also supports racks of up to eight instrument cores in one instance, with individual mixing, MIDI channels, key and velocity splits, and rack presets.

Pricing & Availability:

Retromulator and OB-Xd 4 are available now for macOS, Windows and Linux. Introductory pricing is $99 each through December 31, 2026, increasing to $199 afterward.

Other additions include an arpeggiator with host tempo synchronization, chord memory, MPE support and MIDI Learn. A built-in USB librarian provides two-way editing with an OB-X8 hardware synthesizer, as well as bank transfer, backup, restore and operating system updates.

Retromulator 2.4

The Retromulator update adds two new instrument cores. Nordic 2 recreates the Clavia Nord Lead 2 without requiring its original firmware or ROM data. It offers 64 voices, compared with the hardware’s 16, four-part Performance mode and compatibility with Nord Lead 2 and N2X banks.

MiniD is a three-oscillator analog monosynth recreation based on measurements of hardware. It includes a transistor ladder filter, filter and loudness contours, and polyphonic, unison and double-voice modes.

Retromulator also supports racks of up to eight instrument cores in one instance, with individual mixing, MIDI channels, key and velocity splits, and rack presets.

Pricing & Availability:

Retromulator and OB-Xd 4 are available now for macOS, Windows and Linux. Introductory pricing is $99 each through December 31, 2026, increasing to $199 afterward.

title: Nvidia-Debatte: Solidaritätswelle der Tech-Bros – Wie das Silicon Valley für eine Rückkehr von Jensen Huang lobbyiert
subtitle: Vier Tage nach der Absetzung des Nvidia-Chefs nimmt die Kampagne zu seiner Wiedereinsetzung an Fahrt auf.
feedText: Jensen Huang: Er trat auf Druck des Verwaltungsrats als Nvidia-Chef zurück. Foto: Julia Demaree Nikhinson/AP/dpa Menlo Park, München. David Sacks nimmt kein Blatt vor den Mund. Der zurückgetretene Nvidia-Chef Jensen Huang habe eine genauere Aufklärung der Vorwürfe gegen ihn verdient. „Er hat das Recht, dass Vorwürfe gegen ihn vor einem ordentlichen Gericht geklärt werden“, sagte Sacks, einflussreicher Wagniskapitalgeber und früherer KI- und Kryptoberater von US-Präsident Donald Trump , bei einer Veranstaltung des US-Medienunternehmens Semafor im Silicon Valley . articleBody:
# Nvidia-Debatte: Solidaritätswelle der Tech-Bros – Wie das Silicon Valley für eine Rückkehr von Jensen Huang lobbyiert

Jensen Huang: Er trat auf Druck des Verwaltungsrats als Nvidia-Chef zurück. Foto: Julia Demaree Nikhinson/AP/dpa Menlo Park, München. David Sacks nimmt kein Blatt vor den Mund. Der zurückgetretene Nvidia-Chef Jensen Huang habe eine genauere Aufklärung der Vorwürfe gegen ihn verdient. „Er hat das Recht, dass Vorwürfe gegen ihn vor einem ordentlichen Gericht geklärt werden“, sagte Sacks, einflussreicher Wagniskapitalgeber und früherer KI- und Kryptoberater von US-Präsident Donald Trump , bei einer Veranstaltung des US-Medienunternehmens Semafor im Silicon Valley .

Die Öffentlichkeit sollte „abwarten, bis eine ordnungsgemäße Entscheidung der Justiz“ zu den Vorwürfen vorliege. Auf die Frage, ob Huang sofort zu Nvidia zurückkehren sollte, legte sich Sacks nicht fest. Zunächst müsse geklärt werden, was tatsächlich geschehen sei. „Es gibt noch zu viele offene Fragen“, so Sacks weiter. Dennoch wurde im Verlauf des Auftritts klar, wem seine Sympathie gehört: Huang.

Sacks ist einer von immer mehr Gründern und Tech-Managern im Silicon Valley, die öffentlich für Huang werben . Auf derselben Veranstaltung sprach sich auch Investor Bill Ackman für eine Neubewertung aus. „Eigentlich gilt die Regel, dass man unschuldig ist, bis die eigene Schuld bewiesen ist. Bei unserer heutigen Presse hat man das gefühlt, es ist genau umgekehrt“, so Ackman.

title: Introducing spatial CSS: A developer preview
subtitle: Safari on visionOS 27.3 comes with an important update: a limited feature preview of the proposed spatial CSS API, with an initial focus on working…
feedText: Safari on visionOS 27.3 comes with an important update: a limited feature preview of the proposed [spatial CSS API](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-spatial-1/), with an initial focus on working with 3D objects through the element. While it’s a big conceptual jump, spatial CSS itself is made of a lot of small tweaks to existing syntax. Read on for more details, but here’s a list of each of the features covered in the update: - Collecting multiple elements inside a spatial: portal - transform to move multiple models independently - position-anchor to snap models together - @environment-map syntax to reuse and manage different lighting, - Enabling orbit over the portal scene with portal-action:orbit, - Using requestVolumetricScene() to launch a connected volumetric scene. You can [experience the spatial CSS demo page here.](https://webkit.org/demos/webkids-puzzle-playground/index.html) You can also learn more about [installing additional simulators from Xcode here.](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/safari-developer-tools/installing-xcode-and-simulators) ## The big picture The 3D element, now available in Safari 27 on all platforms, allows you to present intrinsically 3d objects on their own, in their own space. However, the web is at its best when it allows the **composition and configuration**of content based on author intentions and user context.
articleBody:
Safari on visionOS 27.3 comes with an important update: a limited feature preview of the proposed [spatial CSS API](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-spatial-1/), with an initial focus on working with 3D objects through the <model> element. While it’s a big conceptual jump, spatial CSS itself is made of a lot of small tweaks to existing syntax. Read on for more details, but here’s a list of each of the features covered in the update:

- Collecting multiple elements inside a spatial: portal
- transform to move multiple models independently
- position-anchor to snap models together
- @environment-map syntax to reuse and manage different lighting,
- Enabling orbit over the portal scene with portal-action:orbit,
- Using requestVolumetricScene() to launch a connected volumetric scene.

To enable the features for yourself on Vision Pro, or to check it out in the visionOS Simulator, go to

**Settings**>**Apps**>**Safari**>**Advanced**>**Feature flags**>**CSS Portals**.

You can [experience the spatial CSS demo page here.](https://webkit.org/demos/webkids-puzzle-playground/index.html) You can also learn more about [installing additional simulators from Xcode here.](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/safari-developer-tools/installing-xcode-and-simulators)

## The big picture

The 3D <model> element, now available in Safari 27 on all platforms, allows you to present intrinsically 3d objects on their own, in their own space. However, the web is at its best when it allows the **composition and configuration**of content based on author intentions and user context. These context cues can include the device display capabilities, window size, and color theme. These requirements will remain**even as we include spatial content** — and ideally, authors should be able to use the same kinds of patterns to build for the spatial web.

And spatial *content* should not just be designed for spatial *devices*. The last few years have seen a dramatic rise in the number of websites showing 3D content – on phones, tablets and computers as well as headsets. Spatial web standards should support designing **for browsers wherever they run**.

### New web features, classical CSS

Even better, the numerical parameters can be animated and transitioned in the same way that any other value can be changed on the page.

visionOS 27.3 offers the first components of spatial CSS in a developer preview, and this article demonstrates how to use them through the case study of a simple set of children’s blocks.

## Feature breakdown

### spatial: portal

The feature that kicks this all off is the declaration that an element is acting as a *portal*, through the new spatial:portal syntax. Elements that can contain other elements – think <figure>, <div> – can act as a portal, and will then act as a space that all of the child elements nested inside it share. This preview focuses on model elements, but the specification is written so that this approach should work for all content.

### spatial transform:

Once the models are collected inside a shared space, you can then move, rotate, and scale them using their standard transform attribute. This takes the same DOMMatrix class that creates 2D and pseudo-3D transforms in other contexts, but can now act as a *true* 3D transform to objects inside the portal context.

A simple scene of shaped blocks and a board to slot them in.

< div class = "world" style = "spatial:portal;" >
< model id = "board" src = "board.usdz" > </ model >
< model id = "octagon" src = "octagon.usdz" > </ model >
< model id = "star" src = "star.usdz" > </ model >
</ div >
< style >
</ stye >

The code for presenting this scene and setting the blocks off to the sides.

The board and the block objects can be moved and rotated independently — an expanded settings panel shows different values. While a model’s animation timeline could manage single sequence of action, this adds the degrees of freedom required for more sophisticated interaction or configuration.

### position-anchor

Fitting 3D objects together can get complicated. We need a way to attach models to specific places on other models — think of putting together pieces of furniture. Model is a [void element](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Glossary/Void_element), which means it means we can’t nest models *inside* other model elements the same way that other DOM is nested. Instead, we’re borrowing from the CSS concept of position-anchor and adding a way to align and orient objects according to their anchors. position-context: anchor is the way to make it work.

#### See it in action

The scene presented earlier with the octagonal block slotted exactly into place.

< div class = "world" >
< model id = "board" src = "board.usdz" > </ model >
< model id = "octagon" src = "octagon.usdz" > </ model >
< model id = "star" src = "star.usdz" > </ model >
</ div >

< style >
</ style >

The code for using position-anchor to achieve the correct placement for the block.

The board used in the example consists of three separate objects inside the 3D program it was built within: The visible shape of the board itself, and two *reference* positions — often called “null objects” or “empties” in 3D editors. These correspond to the correct position for each of the shape blocks to slot into when they’re on the board. Here’s the scene and its contents inside Blender:

The default view of the block scene presented inside Blender. Note both the block objects and the target objects in-place on the board.

Rather than copy-pasting values from your 3D editor, or having to guess at the right transform, you can nominate specific anchor points — just like in the 2D equivalent of the feature — to place an object in the right location. These anchor points can be animated, too, making it easier to compose elements even when they’re moving around.

### @environment-map

An environment map is the lighting that is reflected off of an object — think of it as the room that an object appears within.

We introduced environment maps as an HTML attribute on the model element, because it was the only element that would be able to use it. Now that there is a broader range of elements that will be able to *share* environment maps. Taking inspiration from @keyframes for animation, we leverage @environment-map to facilitate this. This preview provides support for 360º HDR images and adds the clarifying syntax to indicate what they are and how to work with them.

#### See it in action

The scene showing a spooky-colored underlighting effect.

< div class = "world spooky" >
<!--... -->
</ div >
@ .world The code for setting up the spooky environment lighting.

### portal-action:orbit

One of the main things that users want to do with 3D content is to look around it by rotating the scene in-place. In 3D programs this is often called an ‘orbit’, and spatial CSS enables it with the new portal-action attribute. It may be useful to add more modes in the future like pan-x or pan-y. This mirrors the model element’s stagemode attribute on the HTML element, but by configuring it in CSS it becomes more flexible.

### requestVolumetricScene()

In addition to showing a spatial arrangement inside a portal, visionOS has the ability to show these scenes *outside* of the browser window in what we’re calling a Connected Volumetric Scene. Launch a request from a user action to remove the spatial content from its portal and present it in the user’s space:

launchSpaceButton. addEventListener ( "click", event = > {
const world = document. querySelector ( ".world" );
world. requestVolumetricScene ();
});

The code to launch the volumetric scene.

Users can place the volumetric scene anywhere in their space, and the live link between the web page and the volumetric scene will let you update the scene — add or remove objects, or move them based on your needs.

### Your feedback is essential

There is a long journey ahead, and a lot more to get to in the [proposed spatial CSS specification](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-spatial-1/). While this feature preview is limited to visionOS, we thought it was important to release along with the full specification as an indication of how to approach bringing spatial concepts to the web. Along with the general release of the <model> element on Safari 27, we hope this gives authors enough to think about the opportunities — and requirements — that lie ahead in the spatial web. That’s also why it’s so important for authors to **explore the feature preview** and tell us about their experience of using it. You can download the visionOS simulator with Xcode. If you don’t already have Xcode, you can [download Xcode from the Mac app store.](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/xcode/id497799835?mt=12)

To share your thoughts on the Spatial CSS feature preview, find us on Mastodon at [@jensimmons@front-end.social](https://front-end.social/@jensimmons), [@jondavis@mastodon.social](https://mastodon.social/@jondavis), or on X at [@zachernuk](https://x.com/zachernuk). Or send a reply on X to [@webkit](https://x.com/webkit). You can also follow [WebKit on LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/in/apple-webkit/). If you run into any issues, we welcome your feedback about WebKit at [bugs.webkit.org](https://bugs.webkit.org/). Filing issues really does make a difference. Thanks.

To enable the features for yourself on Vision Pro, or to check it out in the visionOS Simulator, go to **Settings**>**Apps**>**Safari**>**Advanced**>**Feature flags**>**CSS Portals**. You can [experience the spatial CSS demo page here.](https://webkit.org/demos/webkids-puzzle-playground/index.html) You can also learn more about [installing additional simulators from Xcode here.](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/safari-developer-tools/installing-xcode-and-simulators) ## The big picture The 3D element, now available in Safari 27 on all platforms, allows you to present intrinsically 3d objects on their own, in their own space. However, the web is at its best when it allows the **composition and configuration**of content based on author intentions and user context. These context cues can include the device display capabilities, window size, and color theme. These requirements will remain**even as we include spatial content** — and ideally, authors should be able to use the same kinds of patterns to build for the spatial web. And spatial *content* should not just be designed for spatial *devices*. The last few years have seen a dramatic rise in the number of websites showing 3D content – on phones, tablets and computers as well as headsets. Spatial web standards should support designing **for browsers wherever they run**. ### New web features, classical CSS By routing functionality for spatial content through declarative CSS, a page can use media queries targeting aspect ratio, color theme and reduced motion to adapt spatially as well. This adds much more flexibility to your website without having to do as much in your JavaScript, and removing the need to keep track of any complicated state. Even better, the numerical parameters can be animated and transitioned in the same way that any other value can be changed on the page. visionOS 27.3 offers the first components of spatial CSS in a developer preview, and this article demonstrates how to use them through the case study of a simple set of children’s blocks. ## Feature breakdown ### spatial: portal The feature that kicks this all off is the declaration that an element is acting as a *portal*, through the new spatial:portal syntax. Elements that can contain other elements – think , – can act as a portal, and will then act as a space that all of the child elements nested inside it share. This preview focuses on model elements, but the specification is written so that this approach should work for all content. ### spatial transform: Once the models are collected inside a shared space, you can then move, rotate, and scale them using their standard transform attribute. This takes the same DOMMatrix class that creates 2D and pseudo-3D transforms in other contexts, but can now act as a *true* 3D transform to objects inside the portal context. A simple scene of shaped blocks and a board to slot them in. The code for presenting this scene and setting the blocks off to the sides. The board and the block objects can be moved and rotated independently — an expanded settings panel shows different values. While a model’s animation timeline could manage single sequence of action, this adds the degrees of freedom required for more sophisticated interaction or configuration. ### position-anchor Fitting 3D objects together can get complicated. We need a way to attach models to specific places on other models — think of putting together pieces of furniture. Model is a [void element](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Glossary/Void_element), which means it means we can’t nest models *inside* other model elements the same way that other DOM is nested. Instead, we’re borrowing from the CSS concept of position-anchor and adding a way to align and orient objects according to their anchors. position-context: anchor is the way to make it work. #### See it in action The scene presented earlier with the octagonal block slotted exactly into place. The code for using position-anchor to achieve the correct placement for the block. The board used in the example consists of three separate objects inside the 3D program it was built within: The visible shape of the board itself, and two *reference* positions — often called “null objects” or “empties” in 3D editors. These correspond to the correct position for each of the shape blocks to slot into when they’re on the board. Here’s the scene and its contents inside Blender: The default view of the block scene presented inside Blender. Note both the block objects and the target objects in-place on the board. Rather than copy-pasting values from your 3D editor, or having to guess at the right transform, you can nominate specific anchor points — just like in the 2D equivalent of the feature — to place an object in the right location. These anchor points can be animated, too, making it easier to compose elements even when they’re moving around. ### @environment-map An environment map is the lighting that is reflected off of an object — think of it as the room that an object appears within. We introduced environment maps as an HTML attribute on the model element, because it was the only element that would be able to use it. Now that there is a broader range of elements that will be able to *share* environment maps. Taking inspiration from @keyframes for animation, we leverage @environment-map to facilitate this. This preview provides support for 360º HDR images and adds the clarifying syntax to indicate what they are and how to work with them. #### See it in action The scene showing a spooky-colored underlighting effect. @ .world The code for setting up the spooky environment lighting. ### portal-action:orbit One of the main things that users want to do with 3D content is to look around it by rotating the scene in-place. In 3D programs this is often called an ‘orbit’, and spatial CSS enables it with the new portal-action attribute. It may be useful to add more modes in the future like pan-x or pan-y. This mirrors the model element’s stagemode attribute on the HTML element, but by configuring it in CSS it becomes more flexible. ### requestVolumetricScene() In addition to showing a spatial arrangement inside a portal, visionOS has the ability to show these scenes *outside* of the browser window in what we’re calling a Connected Volumetric Scene. Launch a request from a user action to remove the spatial content from its portal and present it in the user’s space: launchSpaceButton. addEventListener ( "click", event = > { const world = document. querySelector ( ".world" ); world. requestVolumetricScene (); }); The code to launch the volumetric scene. Users can place the volumetric scene anywhere in their space, and the live link between the web page and the volumetric scene will let you update the scene — add or remove objects, or move them based on your needs. ### Your feedback is essential There is a long journey ahead, and a lot more to get to in the [proposed spatial CSS specification](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-spatial-1/). While this feature preview is limited to visionOS, we thought it was important to release along with the full specification as an indication of how to approach bringing spatial concepts to the web. Along with the general release of the element on Safari 27, we hope this gives authors enough to think about the opportunities — and requirements — that lie ahead in the spatial web. That’s also why it’s so important for authors to **explore the feature preview** and tell us about their experience of using it. You can download the visionOS simulator with Xcode. If you don’t already have Xcode, you can [download Xcode from the Mac app store.](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/xcode/id497799835?mt=12) To share your thoughts on the Spatial CSS feature preview, find us on Mastodon at [@jensimmons@front-end.social](https://front-end.social/@jensimmons), [@jondavis@mastodon.social](https://mastodon.social/@jondavis), or on X at [@zachernuk](https://x.com/zachernuk). Or send a reply on X to [@webkit](https://x.com/webkit). You can also follow [WebKit on LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/in/apple-webkit/). If you run into any issues, we welcome your feedback about WebKit at [bugs.webkit.org](https://bugs.webkit.org/). Filing issues really does make a difference. Thanks.

title: Discover this year's Dezeen Awards Designers of the Year
subtitle: Dezeen has announced the six winners of Dezeen Awards 2026 Designers of the Year at this evening's ceremony in London, which include Lina Ghotmeh,…
feedText: Our Designers of the Year awards recognise the best emerging and established talent whose innovative work has made a notable impact on the industry across architecture, interiors and design. This year, Ghotmeh took home the architect of the year award, while studio duo Shohei Kuma and Elsa Escobedo were named emerging architect of the year. Interior designer of the year was awarded to Tokyo-based Ashizawa, and Australian designer Yasmine Ghoniem was named emerging interior designer of the year. London-based Ilor…
articleBody:
Dezeen has announced the six winners of Dezeen Awards 2026 Designers of the Year at this evening's ceremony in London, which include [Lina Ghotmeh,](https://www.dezeen.com/tag/lina-ghotmeh/) [Keiji Ashizawa](https://www.dezeen.com/tag/keiji-ashizawa/) and [Yinka Ilori](https://www.dezeen.com/tag/yinka-ilori/).

Our Designers of the Year awards recognise the best emerging and established talent whose innovative work has made a notable impact on the industry across architecture, interiors and design.

This year, Ghotmeh took home the architect of the year award, while studio duo Shohei Kuma and Elsa Escobedo were named emerging architect of the year.

Interior designer of the year was awarded to Tokyo-based Ashizawa, and Australian designer [Yasmine Ghoniem](https://www.dezeen.com/tag/ysg-studio/) was named emerging interior designer of the year.

London-based Ilori won designer of the year with Stockholm-based [Simon Skinner](https://www.dezeen.com/tag/simon-skinner/) named emerging designer of the year.

Read more about the Designers of the Year below:

> Her poetic approach to materials, memory and landscape brings buildings to life with a rare sensitivity to people, place and planet.

**Architect of the year: Lina Ghotmeh**

Ghotmeh, who is the founder of architecture practice [Lina Ghotmeh Architecture](https://www.dezeen.com/tag/lina-ghotmeh/), is one of the world's most sought-after architects. Among her high-profile projects was [the 2023 Serpentine Pavilion](https://www.dezeen.com/2023/06/06/dezeen-agenda-features-lina-ghotmehs-timber-serpentine-pavilion/) and she was recently appointed to [renovate the British Museum’s Western Range galleries](https://www.dezeen.com/2025/02/21/lina-ghotmeh-british-museum-renovation/).

"From Beirut to Paris and beyond, Lina Ghotmeh creates architecture that feels both rooted in history and entirely of the future," said the judges.

"Her poetic approach to materials, memory and landscape brings buildings to life with a rare sensitivity to people, place and planet. We anticipate her studio continuing to go from strength to strength."

Ghotmeh is known for her sustainable and historically rooted designs, including the [Stone Garden apartment block in Beruit](https://www.dezeen.com/2021/11/22/stone-garden-lina-ghotmeh-architecture-project-year-dezeen-awards-2021/), which was named [architecture project of the year](https://www.dezeen.com/2021/11/22/stone-garden-lina-ghotmeh-architecture-project-year-dezeen-awards-2021/) at Dezeen Awards 2021. She has received multiple accolades, including being named on the [Time100 Next list in 2025](https://www.dezeen.com/2025/10/01/lina-ghotmeh-time100-next-list/) and winning the 2023 Great Arab Minds Award.

[Read more about Lina Ghotmeh](https://www.dezeen.com/?p=2371878)

> Working between Japan and Europe, Kuma and Elsa are creating an architectural vocabulary that feels both regionally distinctive and deeply connected to its surroundings.

**Emerging architect of the year: Shohei Kuma and Elsa Escobedo**

Founded by Japanese architect Shohei Kuma and French‑Spanish architect and urban designer Elsa Escobedo, Kuma&Elsa is an emerging architecture studio with offices in France, Spain and Japan.

"Shohei Kuma and Elsa Escobedo's emerging practice brings a fresh sense of curiosity to architecture, balancing bold forms and material experimentation with tactility and unexpected gestures," said the judges.

"Working between Japan and Europe, Kuma and Elsa are creating an architectural vocabulary that feels both regionally distinctive and deeply connected to its surroundings."

Among the studio's varied and intriguing work is Nakano House in Japan’s Fukuoka prefecture – an apartment block informed by the design of a traditional Japanese engawa.

[Read more about Shohei Kuma and Elsa Escobedo](https://www.dezeen.com/?p=2371894)

> His distinct spaces reveal the beauty in restraint, proving that the most powerful interiors are often those that will quietly stand the test of time.

**Interior designer of the year: Keiji Ashizawa**

Interior designer [Ashizawa](https://keijidesign.com/) runs his interdisciplinary, craft-oriented studio based on the ideal of “honest design”. Along with interior spaces, his Tokyo-based studio designs everything from lighting to furniture and products.

"Prolific designer Keiji Ashizawa brings a quiet confidence to interior design, where natural materials, considered details, refined craftsmanship and a sense of calm take centre stage," said the judges.

"His distinct spaces reveal the beauty in restraint, proving that the most powerful interiors are often those that will quietly stand the test of time."

Recent work from the studio includes a [tea shop in central Shanghai](https://www.dezeen.com/2026/10/23/shanghai-tea-shop-basao-rockbund-historic-buildings/), a [holiday home clad in charred cedar](https://www.dezeen.com/2026/09/11/keiji-ashizawa-house-yatsugatake/) in central Japan and a showroom for Japanese furniture brand [Karimoku](https://www.dezeen.com/tag/karimoku/).

[Read more about Keiji Ashizawa](https://www.dezeen.com/?p=2371900)

> Often challenging convention, her interiors are expressive and distinctive, and full of character, warmth and individuality that defy easy categorisation.

**Emerging interior designer of the year: Yasmine Ghoniem**

Australian designer Ghoniem has found great success since founding her interior studio YSG in 2020 with the aim of creating bold, holistic design experiences.

"Yasmine Ghoniem takes a bold, instinctive approach to interior design, bringing together rich textures, unexpected colour and cultural references," said the judges.

"Often challenging convention, her interiors are expressive and distinctive, and full of character, warmth and individuality that defy easy categorisation."

Among her recent – and varied – designs are a wellness hotel in Bali, the revamp of a Sydney apartment, a warehouse conversion in Sydney designed to evoke the Mojave desert and a bar for gin brand Four Pillars.

[Read more about Yasmine Ghoniem](https://www.dezeen.com/?p=2371930)

> Rooted in his British-Nigerian heritage, his exuberant work reminds us that design can be as joyful as it is meaningful, bringing people together through shared experiences and bold creative expression.

**Designer of the year: Yinka Ilori**

Ilori designs pavilions, installations, pop-ups, products and furniture, all united by a bold use of colour informed by his Nigerian heritage.

"Yinka Ilori injects design with an irresistible dose of colour, humour and optimism, turning everyday objects and spaces into lively celebrations of culture and community," said the judges.

"Rooted in his British-Nigerian heritage, his exuberant work reminds us that design can be as joyful as it is meaningful, bringing people together through shared experiences and bold creative expression."

Ilori has designed numerous pavilions, including the [Colour Palace in London](https://www.dezeen.com/2019/06/11/yinka-ilori-and-pricegore-reveal-colourful-dulwich-pavilion/) and an [events space for the Estrel Berlin hotel](https://www.dezeen.com/2022/06/22/yinka-ilori-pavilion-estrel-berlin/) in Germany. On a smaller scale, he has designed products including [a watch for Swiss brand MB&F](https://www.dezeen.com/2025/08/27/yinka-ilori-watch-mad-editions-grow-your-dreams-mbf/) and his own range of branded homeware.

He also recently created [an extensive collection of furniture, fabrics and homeware for Dunelm](https://www.dezeen.com/2026/07/08/yinka-ilori-dunelm-collection/).

[Read more about Yinka Ilori](https://www.dezeen.com/?p=2371940)

> Simon Skinner is a burgeoning talent who brings a fresh perspective to contemporary Scandinavian design, pairing a thoughtful approach to materials with a refined, understated visual language.

**Emerging designer of the year: Simon Skinner**

Swedish designer Skinner is well-known for his furniture, sculpture and installations that explore how materials can be rethought or reused.

"Simon Skinner is a burgeoning talent who brings a fresh perspective to contemporary Scandinavian design, pairing a thoughtful approach to materials with a refined, understated visual language. His work subverts the familiar, creating distinct new objects that hint at an exciting new direction for design."

Recent examples of his varied, multidisciplinary work include a range of [sculptural lights made from second-hand bowls, ashtrays and cat figurines](https://www.dezeen.com/2026/02/05/simon-skinner-buke-lamps/).

[Read more about Simon Skinner](https://www.dezeen.com/?p=2371959)

**Dezeen Awards 2026 in partnership with Trimble**
Dezeen Awards is the ultimate accolade for architects and designers worldwide. The ninth edition of the annual awards is in partnership with global technology company [Trimble](https://www.trimble.com/blog/trimble/en-US/article/trimble-sponsors-dezeen-awards?utm_source=trimble-website&utm_medium=article). Through connected hardware and software solutions, Trimble helps designers to transform the way they shape spaces and buildings as well as drive productivity in the process. Trimble’s collaboration with Dezeen Awards demonstrates its ongoing commitment to inspiring and supporting creative excellence across the globe.

# Hacker behind 2022 GTA VI leaks pleads guilty

- Gaming
- Entertainment
- News
## Hacker behind 2022 GTA VI leaks pleads guilty

Arion Kurtaj leaked 90 videos of GTA VI years before its release.

Arion Kurtaj leaked 90 videos of GTA VI years before its release.

Arion Kurtaj, a member of the Lapsus$ cybercrime group who leaked 90 videos of Grand Theft Auto VI in 2022 and hacked other big companies, pleaded guilty on Monday, according to the UK’s Crown Prosecution Service (CPS).

Kurtaj, who is now 21, hacked BT/EE sometime between August and November 2021, and starting in early November of that year, the company “noted a marked increase in unauthorised SIM swaps of their customers mobile phones.” He was charged for those offenses and moved to a hotel for his “own protection” in September 2022, but “breached his bail conditions to carry out further hacks on major companies using a mobile phone, the hotel TV’s Wi-Fi and a firestick,” including hacks on Rockstar Games, Uber, and Revolut, the CPS says.

He was sentenced to life in a secure hospital in December 2023 because of his autism, but in January, Kurtaj was deemed fit for trial and moved to prison, the BBC reports .

Kurtaj is set to be sentenced on November 23rd. GTA VI will be released on November 19th.

- Jay Peters
